title: Regional normalization and continuous validation for Redwood-verified performance profiles
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: We publish Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) used by runtime routing, Dedicated capacity sizing, and customer billing estimates. Current profile publishing assumes a single canonical region and hardware stack which causes variance for customers in other regions and for different GPU types. This ticket defines a pipeline to normalize regional differences, automate continuous validation against a telemetry contract, and surface region- and hardware-tagged profiles with clear pin/rollback semantics.

Goals: 1) Produce verified profiles that are comparable across regions and representative of production tail behavior. 2) Automate periodic revalidation (daily smoke + weekly regression) and force a gated rollback if regressions exceed SLOs. 3) Expose region/hardware tags and a normalized cost-per-token metric in the profile catalog so customers and routing policies can make consistent decisions. 4) Keep manual intervention minimal; provide clear runbook and audit trail for profile publishes.

Approach: - Telemetry contract: define a minimal set of input prompts, sequence lengths, and concurrency shapes (including synthetic tail-latency spikes) that every benchmark must run. Contract includes accepted percentile thresholds (p50/p95/p99), throughput at target batch sizes, and cost-normalization formula that accounts for GPU type and spot vs reserved pricing. - Regional normalization: implement a post-processing step that collects raw latencies from each region/hardware run and computes a normalized profile relative to a baseline region (us-west-2 with A100-80GB). Normalization factors are published with the profile metadata. - Continuous validation pipeline: nightly smoke tests (sanity and warm-up) and weekly full benchmarks. Automated regressions open a flagged release in the catalog and trigger canary routing to fallback model variants until a fix is published. - Pinning & rollback: when a new profile is published, it is initially tagged as "staged" for 24 hours and routed to 10% traffic by default. If no regressions are observed, the profile is promoted and pinned for production routing. Rollback is automated if p99 latency increases beyond the rollback threshold in two consecutive checks.

Acceptance criteria: - New profiles include region and hardware tags and a normalized cost-per-token field. - Pipeline runs end-to-end with synthetic tail-latency scenarios and publishes an artifacts bundle (raw traces + normalized metrics). - Canary promotion works: staged profiles route to 10% traffic and auto-promote or auto-rollback based on validation gates. - Documentation: Confluence publish of telemetry contract, normalization algorithm, and runbook. - Dashboard: Console shows per-profile region deltas and a link to the artifact bundle for audits.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: Normalization hides real regional degradations. Mitigation: surface both raw and normalized metrics and require sign-off for any normalization factor change. - Risk: Cost formula drifts with cloud price changes. Mitigation: schedule monthly price refresh and include pricing source link in profile metadata.

Stakeholders: PM (Ava Patel), Eng owners: runtime-performance (Liam Chen), infra (Priya Kumar), Observability (Jared Moore), Design: Erika Soto.

Estimated effort: 2 sprints (pipeline + runbook) + ongoing maintenance (automation of weekly revalidations).
